title: Accounting Agents research corpus
mission: A public, read-only research corpus that helps people and agents find, understand, and reuse the information needed to build accounting agents.
coverage_note: Local AA-I102/AA-I103 integration 2026-09-18.102103: the verified 2026-09-18.1 corpus is extended with one official US gift-card authority, one combined synthetic wholesale and retail reconciliation fixture, additive FASB source-review history, a US-scoped revision of six existing trade questions, and two partial industry assessments for NAICS 42 and 44-45. The package covers merchant versus broker or marketplace roles, consignment, returns, vendor consideration, landed cost, POS and processor settlement, gift-card liabilities, loyalty boundaries, grocery shrinkage and inventory cutoff. Existing international material remains context only and is not substituted for US authority. Current consolidated Codification, entity contracts, live populations, professional review, operating effectiveness, empirical support and reuse rights remain unresolved where stated.
review_note: The 2026-09-18.102103 edition is a local author package from verified main a38de70787ee47653f3e315a3c31f0577b5b9ae2 on the isolated AA-I102/AA-I103 branch. It preserves the prior 2026-09-18.1 release as the immutable predecessor and adds only the issue-specific source, example, guide, coverage-registry, assessment, mapping and history updates. The two assessments are partial routing and evidence anchors, not findings of industry or accounting sufficiency. Source review used official issued FASB amendments and the Census NAICS manual, while current consolidated text, entity-specific contracts and operational populations remain unreviewed. This local preparation does not publish, merge or close AA-I102 or AA-I103.
rights_note: Project-created factual metadata is CC0 1.0. Original editorial content is CC BY 4.0. Software is MIT. External source content is not redistributed or licensed by this project; access is not permission for training or reuse.
coverage_priorities: Reverify inherited source URLs, editions, effective dates, supersession, and evidence classifications; keep release-specific checks current.
Add jurisdiction-specific accounting, audit, tax, payroll, and public-sector authorities beyond the present US, European and selected other coverage.
Deepen real transaction-level and ledger evidence, finance-specific CDC/deletion behavior, ERP completeness and reconciliation examples; documented contracts remain untested here.
Add independent empirical deployment studies, incident and failure reports, and reproducible accounting workflow evidence beyond controlled questions and synthetic datasets.
Resolve dataset-specific and upstream permissions, including TabFormer and the FiFAR/BAF interaction; keep unknown rights unknown.

Deepen construction coverage with current consolidated GAAP review, state-specific tax and public-works rules, contract and job-cost datasets, ERP lineage and professional validation; continue other industry guidance including nonprofit and government implementation.
